title: Dickson finiteness and minimal domination
statement: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\mathbf N^n$ the componentwise partial order. For every subset $S\subseteq\mathbf N^n$ and every $a\in S$, there exists $b\in S$ with $b\le a$ such that $c\in S$ and $c\le b$ imply $c=b$. Every antichain $A\subseteq\mathbf N^n$ is finite [def-sfb-finite-infinite-set]; here antichain means that distinct elements are incomparable in the componentwise order.
